column3: Close to the Greek; NKJV names “Jesus” where the Greek has “He.”
NKJV includes “saw him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “having looked up, Jesus said.”
Close to the Greek; “defrauded” is rendered “taken … by false accusation.”
NKJV has “till I come,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “while I am coming.”
NKJV has “how much every man had gained,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “what they had gained.”
Close to the Greek; “a piece of cloth” is rendered “a handkerchief.”
Close to the Greek; “harsh” is rendered “austere.”
NKJV prints this verse in parentheses as an aside; the Greek has no such marking.
NKJV includes “from him” at the end, following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV has “His disciples,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “the disciples.”
NKJV supplies “here” and has “Loose it and bring it,” following the Textus Receptus wording.
